# Version history

- 2026-10-16: moved here from `taxmarker-mislabel-tests.qmd`: the three setups on MislabelBench cells (family distance, 5%, seed 1).

# Summary

This report runs nf-core/taxmarker on cells of the MislabelBench grid [@mislabelbench], a benchmark that relabels 1% or 5% of 2,023 archaeal 16S sequences in groups of k sharing one wrong label.
It complements `taxmarker-mislabel-tests.qmd`, where one wrong-label group is injected into a bacterial reference.
A sequence the pipeline reports as mislabelled is said to be *flagged*.

- With sativa-epang alone, recall of injected sequences falls with k like the figures MislabelBench reports for sativa-epang.
- With clustering in front, the injected sequences that share a cluster with a flagged representative are 64-73% of all injected at k >= 3, against 16-42% for sativa-epang alone.
  That is the opposite of the single-group sets, where clustering lost all injected sequences.
- The price is on the other sequences: expansion adds 58-151 flags, and the share of flags that are injected is lower than for sativa-epang alone at k <= 3 (0.22-0.32 against 0.41-0.63) and higher at k >= 5 (0.25-0.38 against 0.18-0.27).
- Raxtax flags 94 of 101 injected sequences at k = 1, but only 9 of those are sativa-epang flags.

# Results

## The three setups on one cell per k

To see whether the clustering result depends on the injection design, the three setups (sativa-epang alone, clustering with raxtax off, and the pipeline defaults) were run on cells of the MislabelBench grid [@mislabelbench]: family distance, 5% of the 2,023 archaeal sequences relabelled, k = 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 sequences per wrong label, seed 1, plus the un-injected base set.
The input is its alignment and its taxonomy, with `--fast --seed 42` and `GTR+FO+I+R10` as elsewhere in this report (`scripts/run_mb.sh`, run on a 128-core server; results scored with `scripts/mb_cells.py`).
Here 101-110 sequences are injected in groups of k, each group with its own donor and recipient taxon, and no donors are deleted.
Flagged counts every method, so raxtax flags count as well; testable = injected sequences that reach sativa-epang after clustering and raxtax; expanded = injected sequences that are flagged or share a cluster with a flagged representative.
Added = flags on non-injected sequences that are not flagged at the same setup's base run.

```{r tbl-mb-cells}
#| label: tbl-mb-cells
#| tbl-cap: The three setups on MislabelBench cells (family distance, 5%, seed 1; seed 42, lwr > 0.9). Flagged and expanded are injected sequences; added counts flags on other sequences; injected share of flags is flagged injected sequences over all flags, which include the flags of the un-injected base set. Expansion adds every member of the cluster of a flagged representative.

read_tsv("data/mb_cells.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(cell_k > 0) %>%
  mutate(setup = factor(setup, c("alone", "cluster", "cluster_raxtax"), c("sativa-epang alone", "cluster", "cluster + raxtax"))) %>%
  transmute(setup, k = cell_k, injected, testable, flagged, `flagged by sativa-epang` = flagged_sativa,
            expanded = flagged_expanded, added, `added, expanded` = added_expanded,
            `injected share of flags` = round(flagged / (flagged + other_flags), 2),
            `injected share, expanded` = round(flagged_expanded / (flagged_expanded + other_expanded), 2)) %>%
  arrange(setup, k) %>%
  kable()
```

sativa-epang alone flags 86, 73, 43, 17 and 21 of the injected sequences at k = 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 (85%, 72%, 42%, 16% and 19%), a fall with k of the same shape as the one in the single-group sets, and close to the recalls MislabelBench reports for sativa-epang at this distance and rate (0.96, 0.67, 0.49, 0.23 and 0.20).
With clustering in front, only the 28 to 101 representatives are placed, and 18 to 81 of the injected sequences are flagged, fewer than alone at k = 2 and 3 and the same at k = 5 and 10.
Among the representatives the flagged share is 73% at k = 2, 55% at k = 3, 36% at k = 5 and 64% at k = 10.
Counting the cluster-mates of a flagged representative as flagged gives 82, 76, 70, 67 and 80 injected sequences flagged, 64-73% at k >= 3 against 16-42% alone.
The price is on the other sequences: expansion also flags all members of flagged clusters of untouched sequences, and the added flags go from 2-18 to 58-151.
Raxtax flags 94 of 101 at k = 1, but only 9 of those are sativa-epang flags; it removes flagged sequences from the tree before the placement, and the added flags are 8-43 without expansion, against 2-18 for clustering alone.

So the loss of injected sequences with clustering in the single-group sets does not reappear here, where each wrong label is carried by one group among many recipients.
Whether that is because the groups are spread over many recipients, or because the donors here are not the near-identical *S. aureus* sequences of the delete design, has not been tested.
It also means that the clustering result depends on how the injected sequences are spread, which the single-group design cannot show.
Only one cell per k and one run per cell are available, so these are single observations.
